cards.b: Component 2: Pearson sets a broad theme; 72 marks, 50% of the qualification.
Up to four sessions within three consecutive weeks.
Three A2 sheets of supporting studies plus one A2 sheet of final outcome(s).
Photograph it (about four angles, colour) and mount the photos on one side of an A2 sheet.
They must stop when the 10 hours begin; you cannot add to or alter them.
Present a personal and meaningful response that realises intentions and demonstrates understanding of visual language.
Component 2 must continue in the same title as Component 1.
Do the hardest or most important area first, while fresh.
Keep about 30 minutes at the end to step back, check and adjust.
Block in large areas first; add fine detail last.
Fine Art, Graphic Communication, Photography, Textile Design, Three-dimensional Design.
Moves from 'methodical' to 'imaginative' to 'independence and exciting' as marks rise.

short.q: Explain why your final idea should be planned before the 10 hours start.
short.model: Time in the exam is for making; a clear design avoids wasting time and helps you realise your intentions.

short.q: State two rules about preparatory studies during the 10-hour period.
short.model: You can only use your own studies and cannot add to or alter them.

short.q: Write a simple time plan for a 10-hour painting.
short.model: 1h composition, 2h underpainting, 3h main development, 2h refining, 1h finishing, 1h review.

short.q: What does AO4 mean by 'visual language'?
short.model: How you use formal elements such as line, tone, colour and composition to communicate your ideas.
As photographs from about four angles in colour mounted on one side of an A2 sheet.
